findings.title: Pressure, obedience, and continuing care
findings.claim: The sequence places a weighty parent-child bond beside a specific limit on command: pressure may urge the child toward associating partners with God, yet the refusal of that act leaves companionship and good treatment in place. The parent’s prior care deepens the relationship without transferring authority over this demand.
findings.mechanism: The warning in 31:13 names shirk as grave wrongdoing; 31:14 makes parental care concrete through pregnancy, weakness, weaning, and gratitude; 31:15 then conditions the refusal on pressure toward shirk and immediately commands companionship in worldly life. This contact makes the conflict one of bounded allegiance within an ongoing relationship.
findings.reader_payoff: The refusal reads as a limit on this demanded act while the parental relation remains active. The focus’s worldly setting also permits a bounded snare image for the pressure to bind allegiance.
findings.containment: The trap branch is an analogy carried by the focus’s shirk form and activated by its worldly setting and the parental context; it does not make the parents literal hunters or declare every worldly bond a trap. The prohibition is specific to the demanded association, not a withdrawal of all obedience or care.

epistemic.reason: The focus and adjacent ayah surfaces are supplied, and the channel supports are trusted nominations. The trap branch has qualified identity and remains an explicitly bounded analogy.

findings.title: Companionship and the path of allegiance
findings.claim: The pericope lets two relations remain distinct: the child continues good companionship with parents whose care has been made visible, while the path to follow is that of the person who turns to God. The nearby defense of ancestral practice makes that path a concrete choice of allegiance.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins ṣāḥibhumā and maʿrūfan to ittabiʿ sabīla man anāba ilayya. The parental burden and gratitude of 31:14 give companionship a real social object; 31:21 contrasts following revelation with following what was found among the fathers. The later instruction in 31:19 speaks of measured walking, lending the road language an embodied movement cue.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader can see how care for parents remains intact while the direction of guidance is chosen by a different relation to God; the path is both an allegiance and a walkable way.
findings.containment: The contrast does not declare all ancestral practice wrong or cut off the parents. The trace image is qualified: 31:21 reports an inherited practice, not a narrated investigation. The supplied 31:19 text supports measured walking and lowered voice only.

epistemic.reason: The focus and context surfaces are explicit and the channel evidence is trusted nomination material; the inherited-trace relation is interpretive and remains bounded.

findings.title: Parental debt has a boundary
findings.claim: 31:14 makes the parental claim weighty through pregnancy, compounded weakness, weaning, and gratitude. In 31:15 that debt remains honored through companionship even when the child cannot obey the demand toward shirk; the repeated return to God limits both claims.
findings.mechanism: The HFT trace connects the explicit partner warning in 31:13 with the parental instruction, birth, maternal bearing, weakness, weaning, gratitude, and final destination in 31:14. Those context roles meet the focus’s pressure, refusal, companionship, good conduct, and return. The result preserves a before-and-after change from “remain kind despite having to disobey” to a calibrated parental debt whose care persists without transferring allegiance.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus becomes a measure of a real parental bond: refusal does not mean disregard, and care does not make every demand binding.
findings.containment: The source itself offers a live alternative: weaning may be biographical timing rather than a model for the boundary. Keep that connection as an attributed analogy only. The HFT reader identity is legacy_unbound, and its context word coordinates are attributed rather than independently QAC-joined.

epistemic.reason: The HFT’s exact pericope anchors and word-index/root roles contact the supplied Arabic and return to focus words, but the reader identity is legacy_unbound and the weaning-to-boundary step is explicitly an inference.

findings.title: The inherited route as groove and attachment

Its attributed strap and groove branches turn that contrast into a spatial-material analogy of inherited attachment and changed route.
findings.reader_payoff: A bare disagreement becomes a scene of choosing whether to remain fastened to an inherited track or read the way toward God.
findings.containment: The HFT explicitly marks the strap and groove branches as homonymous and branch-distant. This remains an exploratory spatial analogy, not a literal strap or groove, not a claim that every family tradition is wrong, and not an independently verified segmentation of 31:21. The supplied Arabic validates surface contact only.

epistemic.reason: The trace names exact supplied focus and context coordinates and returns to the focus road, but its reader identity is legacy_unbound and its material branches are explicitly surprising analogies.

findings.title: The returning guide turns from wrong
findings.claim: The focus’s anāba ilayya can be heard as a turn away from wrongdoing toward God: the person to follow is not only someone who returns, but one whose direction has turned from a wrong path.
findings.mechanism: The focus’s path-of-the-returner phrase carries an available God-directed repentance branch. The prior warning names shirk as grave wrong, and 31:21 presents inherited practice against following what God sent down; these distinct contextual triggers make the return a change of allegiance rather than a bare return to a destination.
findings.reader_payoff: The path’s guide becomes a model of leaving an inherited wrong and orienting oneself toward God.
findings.containment: The context does not say that every parent or every inherited practice is wrong. The focus’s ordinary sense of turning toward God remains intact; this branch adds the bounded possibility of turning from the specific wrong named in 31:13.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch is present with an exact surface carrier and the supplied adjacent texts provide a specific wrong and an alternative practice; their contact is interpretive but tightly anchored.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişi yanlışından döner ve Tanrı'ya yönelir.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The preceding ayah names shirk as grave wrong; 31:21 contrasts revelation with inherited practice.
branch_activations.activation: The God-directed turn meets those separate warnings and gives the guide’s return a departure point as well as a destination.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The guide is one who turns away from a wrong and toward God.
branch_activations.boundary: The context does not assign the shirk demand to every parent or condemn every inherited way.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişi yaptıklarını içtenlikle yalnız Tanrı'ya bağlar.

findings.title: Knowledge beside inherited practice
findings.claim: The focus’s lack-of-knowledge clause becomes a criterion for following: 31:21 sets revealed guidance beside a group’s decision to follow what it found among its fathers, making evidence and inheritance distinct grounds for a path.
findings.mechanism: The focus word ʿilm carries the knowledge branch, while the later context supplies the separate inherited-practice act. Their contact changes “without knowledge” from a general description of the shirk demand into a pericope-level contrast between a claim with no knowledge and a route defended by ancestry.
findings.reader_payoff: The disagreement is legible as a question of what grounds a path, while the focus still permits care for the parents who hold another view.
findings.containment: 31:21 describes one group’s reply; it does not identify every ancestral practice as baseless. The branch record’s identity is qualified, so this remains a contextual distinction rather than a universal rule about inheritance.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and the exact supplied 31:21 contrast are explicit; the knowledge-versus-inheritance synthesis is an inference, and the lexical branch identity is qualified.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi bilme, tanıma ve gerçeğine uygun biçimde kavrama durumu bilgisizliğin karşıtıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus says the demanded association is something for which the addressee has no knowledge.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 31:21 contrasts following what God sent down with following what the speakers found among their fathers.
branch_activations.activation: That contextual contrast makes the focus’s lack of knowledge a boundary between revealed guidance and an inherited basis.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The path question is framed by what can be known, not only by who exerts family pressure.
branch_activations.boundary: The context does not claim that all inherited practice lacks knowledge.

findings.title: Companionship as responsive support
findings.claim: The focus’s command to accompany the parents can carry protective support as well as continued presence: 31:14 first shows the care that carried the child, then 31:15 returns that relation as good companionship toward the parents.
findings.mechanism: The focus companionship form carries an available support branch. The immediate context supplies pregnancy, weakness, and weaning as concrete acts of care; their contact changes companionship from mere proximity into responsive support within this specific family relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The command can be felt as answering care with care, not simply maintaining a polite distance.
findings.containment: This remains an inferred reciprocal-support reading. The focus does not state a debt calculation or require obedience to the shirk demand, and the support branch is restricted to accompaniment that protects or steadies another.

epistemic.reason: The companionship branch has an exact focus carrier and the supplied 31:14 surface gives concrete care; the specific reciprocity is an inference supported in part by legacy_unbound HFT roles.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kimsenin kendisine eşlik eden bir gözetim ve destek yoluyla korunması çekirdeği oluşturur.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus verb ṣāḥib carries accompaniment.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The 31:14 HFT trace locates maternal bearing, compounded weakness, and weaning; its supplied Arabic gives those acts in the parental relation.
branch_activations.activation: The focus’s instruction to accompany the parents meets the earlier acts of parental care and makes protective support a reciprocal contextual reading.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Good companionship may return care to the parents who previously carried and cared for the child.
branch_activations.boundary: The contextual word indices are attributed; the focus does not expressly say that the child repays a debt or becomes responsible for every need.

findings.title: Return and the report of deeds
findings.claim: The repeated destination to God in 31:14–15, followed in the focus by a report of deeds, permits the final return to be heard at the horizon of judgment beyond ordinary family life.
findings.mechanism: The focus’s marjiʿ carries return; the previous ayah names the destination to God, and the focus places disclosure of deeds after that return. This sequence activates the qualified post-death return branch and changes the return from a general endpoint into an accountability horizon.
findings.reader_payoff: The parental instruction is placed within an eventual accounting, so present care and refusal both matter beyond the immediate disagreement.
findings.containment: The supplied text names a final destination and disclosure of deeds, not a death or resurrection scene. The post-death facet remains qualified and does not add details about resurrection or its timing.

epistemic.reason: The focus and adjacent destination language support final return, while the move to the specific post-death facet is a qualified inference and the contextual HFT source is legacy_unbound.

All three assigned HFT records are legacy_unbound and their packet-scope relation is broader_than_declared_pericope, although every explicit HFT anchor used here lies in 31:12–21. Their readings remain attributed. HFT context word indices and roots are not independently QAC joins; exact Arabic verifies surface contact only.

The reciprocal-seed note for 31:19 describes companionship and a returning path, but the supplied Arabic says to moderate one’s walking and lower one’s voice. The path finding uses only the literal measured-walking cue and does not rely on that note’s broader description.

The HFT alternatives remain live: 31:14’s weaning may be biographical timing, 31:15’s maʿrūfan may be ordinary courtesy, and the O02 strap/groove senses are homonymous, branch-distant analogies. The afterlife-return facet also lacks an explicit death or resurrection scene in the supplied context.
